title: Commands
text: Command line Commands Run yassb in the project folder (the one containing config/ and src/ ). With npm scripts or npx yassb ; with Bun, bunx yassb . yassb build Copy Builds the site for production: pages and scripts minified. --strict exits with code 1 on any error, --clean empties the output first (dot files kept), --out builds into another folder, --json prints { ok, durationMs, out, diagnostics } instead of the logs. yassb watch Copy Builds, serves the site with live reload and rebuilds on every change. --port 0 picks any free port. See Watch mode . yassb serve Copy Serves the output folder as it is, without building, with the same routing as watch . yassb new Copy Creates a project in ./<name> (kebab-case). See Installation . yassb inspect Copy Describes the project without building it: pages, components, data sources, renderers, directives with file and line, translations. A query narrows it down to a file, data source, renderer, directive or translation key. See Working with coding agents . yassb check Copy Builds the site and validates it; exit code 1 on errors. --no-links skips the link check. yassb docs Copy Prints this documentation in the terminal, a topic of it, or the feature catalogue. Help and version Copy An unknown command prints the help and exits with code 1. From code The same operations are available as functions, running in the current folder: Copy

title: Diagnostics

headings.title: Where the file and line point

text: Command line Diagnostics Every problem YASSB finds has a stable code, the source file, the line and a hint. People read them in the terminal, agents in JSON. Copy Where the file and line point Pages are processed as copies in the output folder, but problems point to your sources: the page in src/app/pages , the component that contains the directive, the template, or the Markdown file of a generated page. A problem reported for a component and again for the page that includes it is shown once. What fails a build Level Exit code fatal errors : your code threw, the configuration does not load, invalid JSON, a broken stylesheet 1 other errors : missing data source, unknown renderer, unresolved url-to … 0, or 1 with --strict / strict: true warnings 0 Missing translations are collected and summarised in one line; yassb check lists them. As JSON Copy Copy Every code is listed, with the features that report it, in the diagnostics reference , and in the terminal with yassb docs diagnostics .

title: Watch mode

headings.title: Live reload and the error overlay

text: Command line Watch mode yassb watch builds the site, serves it, and rebuilds whenever a file changes. Your browser reloads by itself, and errors show up on the page. What is watched The whole project, except the output folder, node_modules , .git and temporary files of editors. That includes the configuration, your renderers and directives, package.json and tsconfig.json . Every build is fresh Each rebuild runs in a new process. Nothing is cached between builds, so: changes to the configuration and to the code it imports are always picked up; if your code throws, the error is printed and shown in the browser, and the server keeps running: fix the file and save. Only what changed is rebuilt You change YASSB rebuilds a stylesheet the styles only; the browser swaps the CSS without reloading a file used only by the scripts the scripts only pages, components, data, translations, Markdown the pages (and the styles, when a custom stylesParser such as Tailwind scans them) configuration, site code, package.json , anything outside src everything Changes made while a build is running are queued into one more build. Live reload and the error overlay Pages get a small script, injected before </body> , connected to the dev server: a badge shows while a rebuild runs; the page reloads when it is done (or only the CSS is swapped); the errors of the last build appear in an overlay at the bottom of the page, with code, file and line, and disappear when fixed. The Content-Security-Policy meta tag is removed in watch mode so that the script can run. Pages are not minified. The dev server http://localhost:3000 , or devServerPort , or --port ; if the port is busy the next one is used. /<lang>/… serves <out>/<lang>/… ; other paths are looked up in the first language, then in the output root; folders redirect to a trailing slash and serve their index.html ; unknown paths serve the home page. One process per output folder Two YASSB processes writing the same output folder would overwrite each other's files and leave empty or mixed pages. So only one at a time may write it: build and check hold a lock during the build, watch for its whole session. Start a second one on the same folder and it stops at once, writes nothing and exits with code 1: Copy The lock lives in the temporary folder of the system, never in the output, so it is never deployed. A lock left by a process that no longer exists (a crash, kill -9 ) is taken over automatically. Different folders never conflict: yassb build --out preview works while watch runs. Warning The dev server is for development only. Deploy the output folder of yassb build to a static host.

title: Build pipeline
text: Core concepts Build pipeline Every build runs the same steps in the same order. Custom code can rely on it. The steps Load the configuration, set folders and languages, run beforeBuild . Copy src/assets to the output; start bundling the scripts in the background. Generate pages from Markdown ( generate-from-files templates). For each language, in alphabetical order: copy every file of src/app/pages to <out>/<lang>/ ; list every file of the output as URLs (used by url-to , written to sitemap.xml ); process each HTML page: components → front matter → built-in directives → custom directives → translation . Post-process every HTML file of the output: front matter placeholders → postProcessors → minification (or the live-reload script in watch mode). Compile the stylesheet, write the scripts bundle. Run afterBuild . A directive still in a page after step 4 is reported as DIRECTIVE_UNPROCESSED : its content is missing. Consequences Translation runs after every directive, so HTML produced by renderers is translated too. Post processors see the final, translated page: the place for URL rewriting, metadata, analytics. Custom directives run on components first and on the page last. The output folder is not emptied between builds unless cleanOut is on. Post processors Copy They run in order, on every HTML file of the output, in build and in watch . A post processor that throws or returns something other than a string fails the build ( POST_PROCESSOR_FAILED ). Minification yassb build minifies every page with html-minifier-terser . The default ( {} ) changes almost nothing; most sites want: Copy yassb watch never minifies. A page the minifier cannot parse is written unminified and reported ( MINIFY_FAILED ). Hooks Copy Both run in build and in watch (unlike npm prebuild / postbuild scripts), which makes afterBuild the place for site-specific validations. A hook that throws fails the build ( HOOK_FAILED ). This website uses afterBuild to write the search index of these docs. sitemap.xml Before each language is processed, YASSB lists every file of the output (pages, assets, everything) as URLs. That list is what url-to searches, and it is written to <out>/sitemap.xml . Without siteHost the host is http://fake.host/ and the file is deleted at the end of the build. With siteHost: 'https://example.com/' the file is kept, with your host. With sitemap: false it is never written; url-to keeps working. A post processor can write its own sitemap.xml : it runs after YASSB's.

title: Data and renderers
text:
Core concepts Data and renderers Lists, cards, timelines: anything repeated comes from a JSON file and a renderer. The page says which file it shows, the renderer says how. A data source Copy Data sources live in src/app/data-sources (sub-folders are fine). Keep them as data: records, texts, dates. Which items go on which page, and how many, belongs in the HTML. A renderer Copy Register it in the configuration: Copy Placing it on a page Copy options is JSON written as is inside the quotes and is passed to the renderer. Repeat the directive to show several files; each directive renders one file. Renderer props Prop Content source the parsed JSON sourcePath absolute path of the JSON file options the parsed options attribute lang the language being built ( undefined without translations) currentFilePath the file being processed config the configuration, with absolute folders frontMatterStore front matter of every page, by output path Renderers return a string and never write files. Escape the data you insert into HTML. Emit fixed UI text as English so it gets translated . The JSON file is parsed again for every directive, so a renderer can sort or change its data freely. Built-in renderers basicElement One element per item, with item.description as content ( item.description[lang] with translations). Used when a directive has no renderer. Copy Options: tag (default span ) and attributes ( true writes a bare attribute, false omits it, arrays are joined with spaces). liDateDescription
  • date: description
    • per item, with dates formatted in the current language: Copy Dates can be YYYY , YYYY/MM or YYYY/MM/DD ; end: "-" becomes , translated by your language files. Errors Code When DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND the JSON file does not exist; nothing is rendered DATA_SOURCE_INVALID_JSON the file is not valid JSON; the build fails RENDERER_MISSING no renderer attribute; basicElement is used RENDERER_NOT_FOUND the renderer is not registered; basicElement is used RENDERER_FAILED the renderer threw; the build fails with the location of the directive

title: Pages and components
text: Core concepts Pages and components A page is a plain HTML file. Shared parts live in components and are inserted with the component directive. Including a component Copy The path is relative to src/app/components . Components can include other components, as deep as you need. What can be a component Extension Inserted as .html , .htm HTML, with its directives processed .svg SVG markup (icons, logos) .md , .txt Markdown converted to HTML A component can start with front matter; its values become placeholders of the page that includes it: Copy How components are processed Each component is processed on its own, before it is inserted: its directives run with the component file as the current file, then the result replaces the comment. The page is processed last. This matters for custom directives that need to see the whole page. Per-language components LANG in the path is replaced by the language being built: Copy Prefer one component with translation keys ; use LANG only for content that is truly different per language. When something is wrong A missing file is reported as COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND with the file and line of the directive, and nothing is inserted. A file type that cannot be included is COMPONENT_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT . Components that include each other endlessly stop after 40 levels with COMPONENT_CYCLE . Note Write one directive per line: the directive is matched on a single line.

title: Configuration files
text: Assets and configuration Configuration files The configuration is the default export of config/default.ts . Files for other environments are merged on top. Copy defineConfig only adds types; export default { … } as YassbConfig works too (and does not need yassb-web at runtime). Environments The config folder is read with the same rules as the popular config package, which YASSB 1 used: File Loaded when default.ts always production.ts NODE_ENV=production (or NODE_CONFIG_ENV ) default-2.ts NODE_APP_INSTANCE=2 <hostname>.ts on that machine local.ts always, last Files are merged in that order: objects deeply, arrays and functions replaced. NODE_CONFIG_DIR changes the folder, and NODE_CONFIG (JSON) is merged last. Extensions: .ts , .js , .cjs , .mts , .cts , .tsx , .json . Other formats (YAML, TOML…) are reported and skipped ( CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED_FILE ). TypeScript everywhere The configuration and everything it imports (renderers, directives, helpers) can be TypeScript or TSX, without installing TypeScript: under Node, each file is compiled on its own with esbuild, using your tsconfig.json : __dirname , relative paths and require work as usual, and stack traces point to your TypeScript lines; under Bun, TypeScript runs natively; types are not checked during the build; run tsc --noEmit for that. A syntax error is reported with file and line; a missing package is explained, including packages YASSB 1 used to install for you ( CONFIG_MODULE_NOT_FOUND ). Note In watch mode every build runs in a fresh process, so changes to the configuration and to the code it imports are always picked up.

title: Options
text: Assets and configuration Options Every option is optional. Types come with the package: YassbConfig , or defineConfig() . Option Default Meaning workingDir see Project structure folder names customRenderers {} renderers by name; a name of a built-in replaces it customDirectives [] custom directive classes, run in this order postProcessors [] (html) => html applied to every page at the end ( pipeline ) htmlMinificationOptions {} html-minifier-terser options for build stylesParser Sass your own CSS compiler ( styles ) skipsStyles false no stylesheet esbuildOptions — extra esbuild options for the scripts webpackConfig — legacy: bundle scripts with the site's webpack showdownConverterOptions { tables: true } Markdown options grayMatterOption — front matter options (excerpts) siteHost — public host; keeps sitemap.xml (end it with / ) sitemap true false never writes sitemap.xml cleanOut false empty the output before building (dot files such as .git are kept) strict false any reported error fails the build i18n.allowHtml false insert translations as HTML devServerPort 3000 port of watch and serve username — replaces USERNAME in directives beforeBuild — hook before every build, in build and watch afterBuild — hook after every build, with { ok, diagnostics, out, durationMs, watchMode } cleanOut Without it, files you delete from the sources stay in the output. With cleanOut: true (or yassb build --clean ) the output folder is emptied first, keeping dot files at its root, so a deployment repository in the output folder survives. In watch mode only full rebuilds clean; a styles-only rebuild keeps the pages. strict By default only problems that make the build unusable exit with code 1: exceptions in your code, invalid JSON, a configuration that does not load, a broken stylesheet. Everything else is printed with file and line. With strict: true (or --strict ) every error fails the build. Warnings never do.

title: Styles and scripts

headings.title: Tailwind CSS or any PostCSS pipeline

text: Assets and configuration Styles and scripts One stylesheet entry and one script entry, compiled into versioned files. Sass and esbuild work with zero configuration; anything else plugs in. Styles src/app/styles/styles.scss is compiled with Sass into dist/public/assets/css/styles-<version>.min.css , compressed. Imports are resolved from the file and from the project root, so @use 'node_modules/…' works. A Sass error fails the build with its file and line ( STYLES_FAILED ). Styles are compiled after the pages, so tools that scan your HTML see everything. Tailwind CSS or any PostCSS pipeline Replace Sass with stylesParser , a function that returns the CSS: Copy It receives the absolute entry (twice, for compatibility) and the absolute output path, and must not write the file. This website uses exactly this, with Tailwind CSS 4. skipsStyles: true disables the step. Scripts src/app/scripts/main.ts is bundled with esbuild into dist/public/assets/js/main-<version>.min.js : imports from your files and from node_modules , TypeScript, JSX/TSX (settings from tsconfig.json ); an IIFE for the browser, target ES2018; minified in build , with an inline source map in watch ; process.env.NODE_ENV set to "production" . Bundling starts at the beginning of the build and runs in parallel with the pages. Errors are reported with file and line ( SCRIPTS_FAILED ). Add esbuild options with esbuildOptions : Copy Sites written for YASSB 1 may keep a webpackConfig : it is run with the site's own webpack (install webpack and its loaders in the site). Versioned file names The version comes from your package.json , with dashes: 1.2.0 gives main-1-2-0.min.js and styles-1-2-0.min.css . The asset tags insert the right URLs, so bumping the version busts every cache.

title: Markdown and blogs
text: Content Markdown and blogs Write posts in Markdown with front matter; a template turns each file into a page. These docs are built exactly this way. A post Copy A template Templates live in src/app/pages-to-generate . The generate-from-files directive names the folder of the Markdown files (relative to src/app ): Copy For src/app/pages-to-generate/blog/post.html and src/app/blog/2026/hello.md , the page is written to dist/public/blog/2026/hello.html : template folder, then the sub-folder of the file, then the slug. Rules .md and .txt files are read recursively. The slug is the front matter slug , else the title in kebab-case, else the file name. The directive must be in the template itself, not in a component. Generated pages then go through every other directive, like any page. Empty files are reported ( MARKDOWN_EMPTY ); a folder that does not exist fails the build ( TEMPLATE_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND ); a template without the directive is skipped ( TEMPLATE_NO_DIRECTIVE ). Front matter Values of the front matter replace { name } placeholders, with one space inside each brace, anywhere in the generated page: strings are inserted as they are (not escaped); dates, and the date key, become ISO strings ( 2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z ); other values are inserted as JSON. Components with front matter and custom directives returning data add placeholders too. An invalid date is reported ( FRONT_MATTER_INVALID_DATE ) and inserted as it is. Markdown options Markdown is converted with Showdown . The default options are { tables: true } ; replace them with showdownConverterOptions : Copy Front matter is read with gray-matter . With an excerpt separator, { excerpt } becomes available: Copy Multi-language blogs Only pages inside a language folder are translated. With translations, put one template per language: pages-to-generate/en/blog/post.html and pages-to-generate/it/blog/post.html , each pointing to its own folder of posts. Tip A Markdown file can also be included in a page as a component: <!-- component="intro.md" --> .

title: Translations
text: Content Translations Write the markup once, in your base language, and mark the text to translate. YASSB builds every page once per language. Languages Each JSON file in src/i18n is a language: Copy Languages are processed in alphabetical order. The first one is served at / by the dev server. Without the folder the site has one language and pages go straight to dist/public . Translation files Copy Keys are flat ( "HOME.TITLE" ) or nested objects ( COMMON.READ_MORE ). Marking text Copy Markup Effect data-t="KEY" the content of the element becomes the translation of KEY data-t (empty) the text of the element is the key data-attr-t + alt-t="KEY" sets alt ; works for any <attribute>-t data-t-interpolate {{KEY}} placeholders in the translation are replaced Translation attributes are removed from the output. A missing key keeps the original text; yassb build prints how many keys are missing and yassb check lists them. Translations run last Translation runs after every directive, so renderers can emit translatable markup: Copy Only translated elements are rewritten; the rest of the page is kept exactly as it was. HTML in translations Translations are inserted as text. To allow markup such as <em> or links: Copy Checks yassb check reports keys missing in some language ( I18N_INCONSISTENT_KEYS ), keys used in pages but missing ( I18N_MISSING_KEY ), keys never used ( I18N_UNUSED_KEY ), and translation attributes left in the output ( I18N_UNTRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE ), which happens for pages outside a language folder.

title: Asset tags
text: Directives Asset tags The compiled CSS and JavaScript have the site version in their names. Two directives insert the right tags. Copy becomes, for a site at version 1.2.0 : Copy The text must be exactly <!-- include-styles-src --> and <!-- include-script-src --> . The URLs follow workingDir.styles , workingDir.scripts , stylesOutFolder , scriptsOutFolder and the version of your package.json : bump the version and every page points to the new files, so browsers never use a stale cache. See Styles and scripts for how the files are produced.

title: Custom directives
text: Directives Custom directives A custom directive is a class with a regular expression and an init() method that returns the updated HTML. Use one for layouts or selections that span several data files. Copy Copy What a directive receives Prop Content fileContents the whole HTML, as updated by the previous directives directiveFullString the text matched by your regex for this call fileFullPath the file being processed: a component in src , or the page in the output lang the language being built config the configuration, with absolute folders frontMatterStore front matter of every page init() returns { html, data } : the whole updated HTML, and values that become { key } -style placeholders of the page. Extending YassbBaseDirective copies the props to this.fileContents , this.directiveFullString , this.config , this.lang and this.fileFullPath . Rules to rely on Built-in directives run first, then yours in the order of customDirectives . init() is called once per match , each time with the HTML as updated by the previous call. If the first call replaces every occurrence, the next calls see nothing to do: write directives that are safe to run more than once. Components are processed before the page that includes them. To act only on whole pages, check where the file is: Copy Errors A class without a static regex is skipped ( DIRECTIVE_NO_REGEX ). A directive that throws, or returns no HTML, fails the build with the file and line of the match ( DIRECTIVE_FAILED ).

title: public-file-list
text: Directives public-file-list public-file-list lists the files of a folder of the built site and passes them to a renderer. Use it for download lists, galleries, or an index of generated pages. Copy Copy Rules The folder is relative to the output folder and scanned recursively, in name order. source is [{ absolutePath, absoluteUrl }] ; sourcePath is the scanned folder. The renderer must be registered in customRenderers ( PUBLIC_FILE_LIST_RENDERER_NOT_FOUND otherwise). Only files already in the output are listed: assets (copied first), pages already processed, and every generated page. A folder that does not exist fails the build ( PUBLIC_FILE_LIST_NOT_FOUND ). An index of generated pages Generated pages keep their front matter in frontMatterStore , by output path. This website builds the sidebar of these docs that way: Copy Note To know the current page, write the directive in the page or template itself, not in a component: components are processed with their own path.

title: Directive syntax
text: Directives Directive syntax Directives are HTML comments with attributes. They are replaced when the site is built, so the source stays valid HTML that any editor understands. The built-in directives Directive Does <!-- component="file.html" --> inserts a component ( Pages and components ) <!-- create-from-data-source="file.json" renderer="name" --> renders a JSON file ( Data and renderers ) <!-- public-file-list="folder" renderer="name" --> renders the list of files of an output folder ( public-file-list ) {{ url-to="fragment" }} the URL of a page of the site ( url-to ) <!-- include-styles-src --> , <!-- include-script-src --> the stylesheet and script tags ( Asset tags ) <!-- generate-from-files="folder" --> one page per Markdown file ( Markdown and blogs ) Your own directives are custom directives . Attributes Values are written in double quotes and end at the closing quote: Copy Write a directive on a single line. options options holds JSON, written as is inside the quotes (no escaping needed), anywhere in the directive. Objects and arrays both work: Copy Single quotes work too: options='{"limit":3}' . Invalid JSON is reported as OPTIONS_INVALID_JSON with the file and line, and the options are ignored. LANG and USERNAME Before its attributes are read, every directive has: LANG replaced by the language being built ( en , it …), options included; USERNAME replaced by the username option of the configuration. Copy USERNAME keeps personal paths out of the sources: Copy Copy Warning Without username , USERNAME becomes the text undefined .

title: url-to
text: Directives url-to url-to finds a file of the built site by a part of its path and inserts its absolute URL. Links survive moving files around. Copy becomes Copy How a file is found The fragment (before # ) is compared, ignoring case, with the URL of every file in the output; it also matches in kebab-case and snake_case ( gettingStarted finds getting-started ). With one match, that URL is used. With several, the file closest to the current page wins (fewest folders between them); ties go to an index.html . A warning URL_TO_AMBIGUOUS is printed; silence it with options="{"warning":false}" . With no match nothing is inserted, and URL_TO_NOT_FOUND suggests the closest URL. The anchor ( #install ) is kept. What can be found Every file in the output at the time the page is processed: pages, generated pages, assets. With translations, languages are built in alphabetical order and each language's pages are copied when its turn comes, so do not rely on links to pages of a later language. Within a language, links resolve to the closest file, which is the page of the same language. siteHost and sitemap.xml The list url-to searches is the same one written to sitemap.xml . Links are always root-relative ( /en/about/index.html ). Set siteHost to publish the sitemap with your host: Copy Warning End siteHost with a slash. Without it, url-to produces links starting with // , as in YASSB 1. sitemap: false never writes the file; url-to keeps working.

title: Working with coding agents

headings.title: Errors an agent can act on

text: Getting started Working with coding agents A coding agent needs three things: a map of the project, the rules of the tool, and a way to know whether its change worked. YASSB ships all three in the command line. 1. Get the map: yassb inspect Copy Copy inspect is read-only: it loads the configuration but never runs a renderer or writes a file. Ask about one thing with a query, or get everything as JSON: Copy The manifest lists pages and their output paths, components (transitively), every directive with file and line, data sources with their shape, renderers, custom directives, post processors, hooks, assets and translation keys, plus the problems visible without building (missing files, unknown renderers, invalid options). 2. Learn the rules: yassb docs Copy The guide ships with the package, so it always matches the installed version and works offline. 3. Verify: yassb check Copy check builds the site and then validates it. Besides every problem of the build, it reports translation attributes left in pages, keys missing in some language, keys never used, broken local links, components and data sources nobody uses, and packages your code imports without declaring them. The exit code is 1 when there are errors, so an agent can loop until it is 0. Errors an agent can act on Every problem has a stable code, a file, a line and a hint: Copy yassb build --json and yassb check --json return the same information as JSON. See Diagnostics . Project rules in AGENTS.md New projects include an AGENTS.md (and a CLAUDE.md that points to it) with the commands and the architecture rules of a YASSB site: JSON is data only: never page placement, never UI labels; HTML is UI and placement: each block declares the data it renders; TypeScript is logic: renderers return strings and emit UI text as translation keys; run npm run check after every change. For coding agents A good first prompt: "Run npx yassb inspect , read AGENTS.md, then …". The answer to "where does this come from?" is always a directive you can find with inspect .

title: Installation

headings.title: Add YASSB to an existing folder

text: Getting started Installation YASSB needs Node.js 20 or newer, or Bun. One command creates a working project. Create a project Copy yassb new creates the folder (the name is converted to kebab-case) and refuses to overwrite a folder that is not empty. The starter contains: config/default.ts , the configuration, with one renderer registered; builder/renderers.ts , a typed renderer; src/app/pages/index.html , components, a JSON data source, a Sass stylesheet and a TypeScript entry; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md , the rules of the project for coding agents; yassb-web as a dev dependency. Develop Copy The site is served on http://localhost:3000 and rebuilt on every change, with live reload. See Watch mode . Build Copy The output goes to dist/public , minified and ready to upload to any static host. Run npm run check before deploying: it builds and validates the site. Add YASSB to an existing folder Copy Create config/default.ts and src/app/pages/index.html ; every other folder is optional and created on the first build. Add the scripts to package.json : Copy Note With Bun, run the same commands with bunx yassb … . Builds are a little faster.

title: Project structure
text: Getting started Project structure YASSB works with conventional folders. Every name can be changed with the workingDir option. Copy Pages and output paths Each file in src/app/pages becomes a page: pages/about.html → dist/public/about.html . With translations, each page is built once per language: dist/public/en/about.html , dist/public/it/about.html . Assets src/assets/ is copied to dist/public/assets/ at the start of every build, keeping its structure. Files whose size and modification time did not change are skipped, so rebuilds are quick. Files you delete from src/assets stay in the output until you clean it: set cleanOut: true or run yassb build --clean . Renaming folders Copy Option Default Relative to base the current folder the folder YASSB runs in src src base out dist/public base assets , i18n , app assets , i18n , app src pages , components , dataSources , pagesToGenerate pages , components , data-sources , pages-to-generate app posts app itself app (base of generate-from-files ) scripts , styles scripts/main.ts , styles/styles.scss app scriptsOutFolder , stylesOutFolder assets/js , assets/css out Missing folders are created on the first build, and so are empty script and style entries.

title: Introduction
text: Getting started Introduction YASSB is a static site builder with a simple contract: data in JSON or Markdown, UI in HTML, logic in TypeScript. It is small, fast, and built so that a coding agent can understand a site in seconds and change it without breaking it. Installation Create a project and run the dev server in under a minute. Working with coding agents inspect, check, docs: how an agent finds its way in a YASSB site. Data and renderers Turn JSON into HTML with a TypeScript function. Feature reference Every feature, with syntax, options, rules and errors. The mental model A YASSB site has three kinds of files, each with one job: What Where Written in Data : records, texts, dates, flags src/app/data-sources/*.json , Markdown files JSON, Markdown UI : markup, and what is shown where src/app/pages/ , src/app/components/ HTML with directives Logic : turning data into markup renderers and directives registered in config/default.ts TypeScript Pages are plain HTML. Directives are HTML comments that YASSB replaces when it builds: Copy A renderer is a function that receives the parsed JSON and returns HTML: Copy Because every block of a page declares exactly the data it shows, you can read a page and know where everything comes from, and so can an agent. Why YASSB Built for agents. yassb inspect describes a site with file and line numbers, yassb check validates a change, yassb docs ships the whole guide offline, and every error has a stable code. Small. Five runtime dependencies. Runs on Node.js 20+ and Bun. Fast. esbuild for scripts and TypeScript, a translator that only touches translated elements, in-memory URL lookups. Robust watch mode. Every rebuild runs in a fresh process: changes to the config and to your renderers are always picked up, and a crash in your code shows up in the browser without stopping the server. Multi-language, Markdown, Sass or Tailwind out of the box. For coding agents Starting on an existing YASSB site? Run npx yassb inspect , then read AGENTS.md if the project has one. npx yassb docs prints this documentation in the terminal.

title: Diagnostic codes
text: Reference Diagnostic codes The stable codes of diagnostics . Search for a code on this page or run yassb docs diagnostics . Code Meaning Reported by CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED The configuration (config/*.ts|js|json) or a module it imports threw while loading. behaviour.site-code , config.files CONFIG_MODULE_NOT_FOUND The configuration imports a package that is not installed in the site. config.files CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED_FILE A config file has a format YASSB 2 does not read (yaml, toml, …). config.files UNDECLARED_DEPENDENCY Site code imports a package missing from package.json (it may work only by accident). cli.check COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND A `component` directive points to a file that does not exist. directive.component COMPONENT_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT A `component` directive points to a file type that cannot be included. directive.component COMPONENT_CYCLE Components include each other endlessly. directive.component DATA_SOURCE_MISSING_NAME `create-from-data-source` has no file name. directive.create-from-data-source DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND `create-from-data-source` points to a JSON file that does not exist. directive.create-from-data-source DATA_SOURCE_INVALID_JSON A data source is not valid JSON. directive.create-from-data-source OPTIONS_INVALID_JSON The `options` attribute of a directive is not valid JSON. directive.attributes RENDERER_MISSING A directive has no `renderer` attribute; title: Feature reference
text: Reference Feature reference 58 features in yassb-web 2.0.0. This page is rendered from the feature catalogue that the build of YASSB checks, so it always matches the code. Directives 8 Built-in renderers 2 Configuration 21 Command line 8 Translations 2 Content 2 Assets 4 Extension API 3 Behaviour 8 Directives directive.attributes stable since 1.0.0 Shared attribute syntax of directives: quoted values, JSON options, LANG and USERNAME placeholders. Copy Options options: JSON (object or array) written as is inside double or single quotes, anywhere in the directive. Rules Values end at the closing quote; LANG anywhere in the directive (options included) becomes the current language; USERNAME becomes config.username (the text "undefined" if unset); invalid options JSON is reported and ignored. Errors OPTIONS_INVALID_JSON Related config.username directive.create-from-data-source directive.component stable since 1.0.0 Inserts an HTML, SVG or Markdown fragment from the components folder, recursively. Copy Options The value is a path relative to src/app/components (workingDir.components); LANG and USERNAME are replaced (see directive.attributes). Rules Each component is processed on its own (its directives run with fileFullPath = the component file) before being inserted into the including file; components can nest; .md/.txt components are converted from Markdown; front matter of a component becomes { key } placeholders of the page; a missing file leaves the comment in place (removed by the minifier); more than 40 levels of nesting is reported as a cycle; the regex accepts one directive per line. Errors COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND COMPONENT_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT COMPONENT_CYCLE Related content.front-matter content.markdown directive.attributes directive.create-from-data-source stable since 1.0.0 Renders a JSON data source with a renderer and inserts the resulting HTML. Copy Options renderer: name in customRenderers or a built-in renderer (default basicElement); options: JSON passed to the renderer as props.options. Rules One JSON file per directive, path relative to src/app/data-sources (sub-folders allowed); the file is parsed again for every directive, so renderers may mutate their data; the renderer receives source (parsed JSON) and sourcePath; every occurrence of the same directive text in the file is replaced; a missing file or name leaves the comment (removed by the minifier) and is reported; invalid JSON or a throwing renderer fail the build. Errors DATA_SOURCE_MISSING_NAME DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND DATA_SOURCE_INVALID_JSON Related api.custom-renderers directive.attributes renderer.basicElement directive.generate-from-files stable since 1.0.0 Generates one page per Markdown/text file from a template in pages-to-generate. Copy Options The value is a folder relative to src/app (workingDir.posts); USERNAME is replaced. Rules The directive must be in the template file itself, not in a component; .md and .txt files are read recursively; output is <out>/<template folder>/<file sub-folder>/<slug>.html with slug = front matter slug, else the title in kebab-case, else the file name; front matter placeholders are replaced at once and again in post-processing; generated pages then go through all directives; with i18n only templates inside a language folder (pages-to-generate/en/...) are translated, so a multi-language blog needs one template per language. Errors TEMPLATE_NO_DIRECTIVE TEMPLATE_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND MARKDOWN_EMPTY Related content.markdown content.front-matter directive.include-script-src stable since 1.0.0 Inserts the script tag of the bundled browser script. Copy Options none Rules The text must be exactly <!-- include-script-src -->; the URL follows workingDir.scripts, workingDir.scriptsOutFolder and the version of package.json. Related assets.scripts assets.file-names directive.include-styles-src stable since 1.0.0 Inserts the stylesheet link of the compiled CSS. title: Upgrading from 1.x
text: Reference Upgrading from 1.x Sites written for YASSB 1 build with YASSB 2 without changes, and produce the same pages. What changes is around them. Steps Copy yassb check lists what needs attention, starting with undeclared dependencies. What changed Node.js 20+ or Bun is required. Fewer dependencies. YASSB no longer installs packages it does not need: react, react-dom, fs-extra, cheerio, lodash, moment, webpack, ts-node, typescript and others. If your code imports one of them without declaring it in package.json , the build stops with CONFIG_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and tells you what to install; yassb check reports them in advance as UNDECLARED_DEPENDENCY . esbuild instead of webpack for scripts: same file name, no separate .LICENSE.txt file. A webpackConfig still works if webpack is installed in your site. TypeScript without ts-node : configuration and site code are compiled with esbuild, faster, with the same __dirname behaviour. Watch mode rebuilds in a fresh process, watches the whole project and shows errors in the browser. Fixed options containing arrays ( {"order":["a","b"]} ) were silently ignored and the block disappeared. $$ and $& in content were altered when inserted into pages. basicElement wrote <undefined> elements without a tag option; it now writes span , as documented. An element with both data-attr-t and data-t lost its text translation. Watch mode reloaded the browser before the rebuild was finished. New yassb inspect , yassb check , yassb docs , --strict , --clean , --json , sourcePath in renderer props, nested translation keys, i18n.allowHtml , sitemap: false , cleanOut , beforeBuild and afterBuild hooks, esbuildOptions , defineConfig , the error overlay and CSS hot swap in watch mode, and the feature catalogue .
